clue.text: Oppose the others crossing island

indicators.note: one thing crossing another lies across it, so these letters straddle the island's letters

blocks.note: the rest are the others
IS is a standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone stands against everyone else as they cross over to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The others' is a single idea, the rest; 'crossing' means it straddles the island abbreviation, which splits it near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist something is to stand against it, a plain synonym of oppose.

clue.text: Change the shape of rock festival held in the centre

indicators.note: held in the centre means gripped in the middle, so the festival sits inside the rock word

blocks.note: to reel is to rock or sway
a Mod is a Scottish Gaelic festival of music and poetry

explanation.surface: A rock festival is restyled from the middle out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock festival' reads as one music event but splits into the verb rock and a Gaelic festival, the Mod.
explanation.definitionFit: To remodel is to rework or reshape something, so altering its form.

clue.text: Reject incentive offered by knight

blocks.note: a spur is a stimulus or incentive
N is the chess notation for knight; offered by places it next to the incentive

explanation.surface: Someone turns down an inducement held out by a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn is to reject with contempt, a stronger synonym of turning something down.

clue.text: Trooper willing to persevere

blocks.note: a trooper is a soldier
on as in game or up for it, meaning willing

explanation.surface: A soldier is ready to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is an idiom for carrying on doggedly despite difficulty, which is persevering.

clue.text: Correspond about hospital making one squirm

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the letters for correspond wrap around the hospital

blocks.note: to correspond is to write letters
H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Writing letters about a hospital stay leaves someone uncomfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspond' suggests letters about a hospital stay; here it is just the verb for writing, which takes in the hospital letter near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Writhing is twisting the body about in pain or discomfort, which is squirming.

clue.text: Rugby Union fellow has no right to make a little money abroad

indicators.note: having no right means lacking the abbreviation for right, so it is struck out of the fellow word

blocks.note: RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union
a peer is an equal, a fellow
R abbreviates right

explanation.surface: A rugby player without entitlement tries to earn a bit of cash overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: PEER loses its R to become PEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency unit of India, Pakistan and elsewhere, so a small sum of foreign money.

clue.text: Actress's horrid hat, crumpled

indicators.note: something crumpled is crushed out of shape, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the nine letters of the fodder

explanation.surface: An actress wears an ugly, squashed hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for is, linking the definition to the wordplay rather than marking possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Thora Hird was a much-loved English stage and television performer, famously in Last of the Summer Wine.

clue.text: Most violent end

blocks.note: first meaning: utmost or most severe
second meaning: the furthest point

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings sit side by side with nothing joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme is an adjective for the most severe degree and a noun for the outermost limit.

clue.text: Foolishly tearful in Oxford college, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is told by word of mouth, so we go by how the college name is spoken

blocks.note: Magdalen College, Oxford, is not said the way it is spelt; its spoken form is a word for weepy

explanation.surface: Someone gets weepy and silly while at an Oxford college.
explanation.walkthrough: Magdalen College, Oxford, is famously pronounced 'maudlin'; the word maudlin itself comes from Mary Magdalene, often painted weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Maudlin describes sentimental, self-pitying tearfulness, often after drink, hence foolishly tearful.

clue.text: Nothing at all suppressed over a treatment

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

blocks.note: sat on means suppressed, as in sat on the news
taken as written
usage is the way something is treated

explanation.surface: Nothing whatsoever was kept quiet about a medical procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: SAT ON turns to NOTAS. Not a sausage is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a sausage is a colloquial British idiom meaning absolutely nothing, so it means nothing at all.

clue.text: Murder in West Indies, extremely predictable and senseless

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities of the word, its first and last letters only

blocks.note: WI is the abbreviation for West Indies
the two end letters of predictable
knocked senseless is out cold

explanation.surface: A killing in the Caribbean that was both foreseeable and pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murder' is used as a verb, as in to wipe someone out.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out a person or group is to kill them off entirely, an informal equivalent of murder.

clue.text: Small cart has to turn round by pub and bank

blocks.note: to wheel is to turn round
a bar is a pub
a bank of seats or keys is a row

explanation.surface: A little trolley must swing about beside a pub and a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn round' is not a reversal signal here; it gives a word in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheelbarrow is a small one-wheeled cart pushed by hand, for gardening or building.

clue.text: I'm tense, and hence upset cartoon character

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the preceding words are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: Someone admits to nerves and so is out of sorts, maybe on reading a comic.
explanation.walkthrough: Dennis the Menace is the spiky-haired troublemaker of the British comic The Beano (distinct from the American strip of the same name).
explanation.definitionFit: Dennis the Menace is a famous comic-strip figure, so he is an example of a cartoon character.

clue.text: Rule changed to accommodate married primate

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters of rule are put in a new order
to accommodate is to take in and house, so the rearranged letters hold the abbreviation

blocks.note: rule rearranged, ready to take in a letter
M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A regulation is amended so that a married monkey can be housed.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters have to be split in the middle to make room for the married abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are tree-dwelling animals of Madagascar belonging to the primate order.

clue.text: Napoleon's place in literature?

blocks.note: surface reading: the French emperor's standing in the history of letters
setter's reading: the home of Napoleon the pig in Orwell's novel Animal Farm

explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon looks like the emperor, but he is the boar who takes over in Orwell's Animal Farm; the farm was called Manor Farm before the animals renamed it.
explanation.definitionFit: Manor Farm is the setting of Animal Farm, the farm where the pig called Napoleon lives.

clue.text: Choosy school I have, but admitting the Spanish

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the school word lets the Spanish article inside it

blocks.note: a school of thought is a sect
el is Spanish for the
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A school picky about its intake still lets in Spanish pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks literal but means a sect, as in a school of thought; EL sits after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Selective means picking carefully and rejecting much, just what a choosy person does.

clue.text: Flower people following vehicle

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
a nation is a people; following places it after the vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone presents a bloom to the crowd trailing behind a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The carnation is a popular garden and buttonhole bloom, so an example of a flower.

clue.text: Piece of land shot in pale sun

indicators.note: shot means ruined or worn out, so the following letters are broken up and remade

blocks.note: the nine letters of the fodder

explanation.surface: A photographer captures a stretch of coast under a weak sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests a photograph taken in the light; here it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A peninsula is land almost surrounded by water, jutting out into the sea, so a particular piece of land.

clue.text: One pound sent over in advance for issue

indicators.note: sent over in a down entry means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way
in places the turned letters inside the word for advance

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
to push is to advance

explanation.surface: A pound is paid up front for a magazine issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In advance' looks like paying beforehand, but in is the container signal and advance gives the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: To publish a book or paper is to issue it to the public, as the verb issue means.

clue.text: Travels free to East Sussex, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of each of the words is kept

blocks.note: to rid is to free, as in rid of a burden
the first letters of East and Sussex

explanation.surface: Someone journeys without paying to East Sussex, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like no charge for the trip, but it is the verb rid.
explanation.definitionFit: Rides as a verb means goes on horseback or by vehicle, a synonym of travels.

clue.text: Infected having caught cold? One might doubt it

indicators.note: having caught means holding something inside, so the infected word takes in the letter for cold

blocks.note: a septic wound is infected
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: Is the patient infected after catching a chill? Some would question it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: the answer is the person who doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic is someone inclined to question claims, so a person who might doubt it.

clue.text: Murder at Bengali resort, a notorious danger area?

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it means sort again, so the letters before it are put in another order

blocks.note: the fifteen letters of the fodder

explanation.surface: A killing at a holiday spot in Bengal makes it a place to avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' reads as a holiday destination but splits as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bermuda Triangle is a stretch of the Atlantic legendary for vanished ships and aircraft, hence notoriously dangerous.

clue.text: Make one marry

blocks.note: first meaning: join together into a single whole
second meaning: join in wedlock

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an order to the vicar; the two verbs are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers combining things into a single unit and joining a couple in marriage.

clue.text: Fellow eating very soft fish

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside, so the fellow word swallows the musical letters

blocks.note: a guy is a fellow
pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very soft

explanation.surface: A man tucks into a fish with very tender flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: The guppy is a small, brightly coloured freshwater species popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Picture of one excavation in which silver's found

indicators.note: in which says one thing sits inside the other, so the metal goes within the excavation

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a mine is a dug excavation
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A photograph of a single dig where silver was struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' is a verb here, as in picture the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine something is to form a mental picture of it, so the verb senses match.

clue.text: Dog bred for racing beat favourite

blocks.note: to whip is to beat
a teacher's pet is the favourite

explanation.surface: A racing dog beats the favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The whippet is a slim greyhound-like breed developed for racing and rabbit coursing.

clue.text: Poor actor allowed in play

blocks.note: a ham is a bad, overacting performer
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A weak performer gets permission to appear in a production.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is Shakespeare's tragedy, so it is an example of a play.

clue.text: Harmonious, bar clubs round outskirts of Sydney

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the bar and clubs letters go about the outer letters
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the first and last letters are taken

blocks.note: an inn is a pub, a bar
the first and last letters of Sydney
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Bars and nightclubs ring the suburbs of an Australian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar clubs' looks like nightlife but is two separate pieces, a pub word and the card suit; the Sydney letters go inside the pub word.
explanation.definitionFit: In sync means moving or working together in agreement, which is being harmonious.
